summary.text: An 80-year-old man presented with a left MCA syndrome from left M2 occlusion (last known well 3 h 14 min before arrival, initial NIHSS 6). He had tenecteplase thrombolysis and EVT, with stenting of a left extracranial ICA stenosis and aspiration thrombectomy (TICI2c recanalisation), and tirofiban was started postprocedurally for in-stent platelet aggregation.

One hour post procedure the syndrome worsened (NIHSS 8) with unremarkable observations, BP 116/56 and no fever; CT angiography showed a patent ICA stent and left M2. Further clinical deterioration prompted repeat multimodal CT perfusion that showed extensive hyperdense cortical oedema with contrast enhancement and loss of grey-white differentiation in the left MCA territory, consistent with CIE. Only intravenous fluids were given; Day 2 MRI showed patchy left MCA infarct without haemorrhagic transformation.

He had fluctuating encephalopathy and neurological deficits for 3 days postangiography, then trended to recovery after Day 3, and was discharged to inpatient rehabilitation with residual mixed receptive and expressive dysphasia, NIHSS 1.
Table 1 (row assigned to Case 1) lists right hemiparesis and dysphasia treated with IV fluids; its "improvement in less than 1 day" conflicts with the narrative and is held for review.

summary.text: A 76-year-old woman had successful insertion of a flow-diverting stent for a right ophthalmic artery aneurysm; the procedure was complicated intraoperatively by an air embolus. Left arm weakness (NIHSS 3) was seen postprocedure and she was transferred for hyperbaric treatment.

Despite supportive medical therapy she deteriorated to a complete right MCA syndrome with approximate NIHSS 19 at 8 h postprocedure (BP 150/67, CRP normal, no electrolyte abnormalities). Repeat CT perfusion showed diffuse right hemispheric cerebral oedema consistent with CIE. She needed intubation and ventilation overnight for severe obtundation and was treated with dexamethasone and levetiracetam.
She was extubated on Day 2 with complete resolution of neurological deficits on Day 3, and MRI on Day 4 showed resolution of right hemispheric oedema without infarction.
Table 1 (row assigned to Case 2) lists left hemiparesis and right gaze preference, extubation on Day 2 and normal power on Day 3.

summary.text: A 94-year-old woman presented with a complete left MCA syndrome secondary to left ICA occlusion (initial NIHSS 24) requiring EVT; despite intensive suction thrombectomy significant residual ICA thrombus remained with TICI 2B recanalisation.

At 7 h postprocedure she deteriorated with obtundation and left-sided focal motor seizures (BP 150/85, normal serum electrolytes). Repeat CT brain showed a large established left MCA territory infarction with widespread subcortical white matter oedema and contrast enhancement of the subarachnoid spaces, and dual energy CT excluded subarachnoid haemorrhage.

Given deteriorating clinical state, extensive infarction and pre-existing wishes, life-sustained treatments were withdrawn and she died after 4 days of palliative care; the authors attribute the poor outcome to the large established infarct rather than CIE.
Table 1 (row assigned to Case 3) lists reduced GCS and focal motor seizures, treated with levetiracetam then supportive end-of-life care.
